title: Unwrapping the 2026 Holiday Outlook
summary: Consumers expect to spend more this holiday season. See how inflation, AI shopping and resilient travel demand are shaping the 2026 outlook.
body_markdown:
That could provide another boost for e-commerce, which is already heading into the holidays with momentum. Morgan Stanley Research expects online holiday spending to grow 8-10% from last year, helped by strong purchase intentions among higher-income consumers and growing adoption of AI shopping tools.


“E-commerce has a few things working in its favor this holiday season, from its exposure to higher-income consumers to the growing adoption of AI-powered shopping tools,” says Brian Nowak, head of U.S. Internet Research at Morgan Stanley. “Together, those trends could help drive a strong year for online spending.”


The impact of AI-powered shopping could extend well beyond the holiday season. Morgan Stanley Research estimates that[$30 trillion](https://www.morganstanley.com/insights/articles/agentic-commerce-ai-agents-30-trillion-consumer-spending) in consumer spending across industries including e-commerce and travel could eventually be influenced by AI-powered shopping tools.


### **Airlines Show Resilience**


Higher prices don’t appear to be keeping consumers on the ground. Many airlines have reported healthy demand and continued interest in bookings, adding to expectations for a solid holiday travel season.


“We remain positive on the U.S. airlines heading into the holiday season, with data and management commentary pointing to resilient consumer demand,” says Ravi Shanker, North America Transportation Analyst at Morgan Stanley Research.


The AlphaWise survey points to continued travel demand beyond the holidays, with 59% of consumers planning to travel over the next six months, up from 55% last year.


“Taken together, resilient demand and higher fares could set airlines up for a strong holiday travel period,” Shanker says.


### **Mixed Outlook on the Retail Industry**


The holiday shopping picture has brightened somewhat, with consumers more willing to spend across a range of gift categories this year. Toys have the strongest outlook, improving from -13% last year to roughly flat this year.


For general and food retailers, stronger holiday spending intentions and continued resilience among middle- and higher-income consumers could support growth. But inflation, pressure on lower-income households and an uneven labor market could make for a mixed holiday season.


Morgan Stanley Research expects holiday spending in this part of the retail industry to grow 4-5%, with higher prices driving much of the increase.


The outlook is more challenging for apparel and other softline retailers. Weaker demand heading into the holidays and the possibility of increased discounting could weigh on sales, even as overall holiday spending improves.


Some categories are also facing greater pressure than others. Sports equipment and home and kitchen products have some of the weakest spending intentions this year, while intimate apparel also continues to lag.


“One encouraging sign is that spending intentions improved from last year across a number of categories, even where consumers still expect to spend less overall,” says Simeon Gutman, who covers hardlines, broadlines and food retail for Morgan Stanley Research. “That suggests the holiday backdrop has improved, even if the recovery isn’t uniform across retail.”
